---
title: "Where is the neutral point and the required CG?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
ENTRY_CEILING = 90.0
SOLVE_BUDGET = 15.0
PROBE_POOL = 150.0
PROBE_SPENT = 5.2

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

airplane = get_airplane()
op_point = asb.OperatingPoint(velocity=10, alpha=0)

aero_stab = asb.AeroBuildup(
    airplane=airplane,
    op_point=op_point
).run_with_stability_derivatives()

x_np = aero_stab['x_np'][0]
mac = airplane.wings[0].mean_aerodynamic_chord()
cg_x = x_np - 0.10 * mac
```

::: {.hero}
[`{python} f"{cg_x:.3f} m"`]{.hero-value}
[Required CG location]{.hero-label}
:::

**Answer.** The X-Wing's neutral point sits at $x = $ [`{python} f"{x_np:.3f}"`]{.key} m from the nose reference. For pitch stability, placing the center of gravity at a 10% static margin requires it to be located at $x = $ [`{python} f"{cg_x:.3f}"`]{.key} m.

::: {.callout-tip}
## New user specifications
Asked of the user, 2026-09-24:

1. **static margin: 10% of MAC** — dictates CG placement.
:::

```{python}
#| label: fig-three-view
#| fig-cap: "Three-view of the X-Wing, with the center of gravity and neutral point marked on the top and side profiles."
axs = airplane.draw_three_view(show=False)
fig = axs[0, 0].figure
fig.set_size_inches(8, 8)

for ax in [axs[0, 0], axs[1, 0]]:
    ax.plot([x_np], [0], [0], 'ro', markersize=6, label="Neutral Point")
    ax.plot([cg_x], [0], [0], 'bo', markersize=6, label="Required CG")

axs[0, 0].legend(loc="upper right")
plt.show()
```
